body.heading: Wake up to frost
paragraphs: On a cold, clear morning, look at the windows before the sun melts everything. You may find white patterns that look like tiny ferns, feathers, and forests.
Frost is water that froze straight onto the cold glass. As it freezes, it grows into branching shapes, a little like a snowflake spreading out flat.

body.heading: Look for patterns
paragraphs: No two frost pictures are ever the same. Look for the longest fern. Look for a pattern that reminds you of a tree, a star, or a spider's web.
Touch one fingertip to the glass. Your warm finger melts a clear spot. That is how delicate frost is — it cannot survive warm sunshine or warm fingers.

body.heading: Draw it before it goes
paragraphs: Draw your favourite frost pattern quickly, before the sun melts the whole show. White crayon on blue paper looks just like the real thing.
By breakfast time, the window may be clear again. Frost art is special because it only visits on cold mornings.

takeaway: Frost grows into fern-like patterns on cold glass overnight, and it melts away as the day warms up.
materials: Blue paper if you have it
safetyNotes: Frosty paths can be slippery — walk slowly with your adult and hold hands on icy ground.
screenFreeExtension: Scratch frost patterns into a tray of flour with a fork to practise the feathery shapes.
